Hours after announcing Apple's support for communities affected by wildfires in southern Europe, Tim Cook said the company would also donate to relief efforts following an earthquake in Kumamoto, Japan. Here are the details.

Apple to donate to Japan relief efforts

Apple CEO Tim Cook once again took to social platform X to announce Apple's plans to help communities affected by natural disasters.

Cook said the company is donating to support relief efforts in Japan, adding that the country "holds a very special place in his heart." You can see his full post below:

On Tuesday afternoon, a magnitude 7.1 earthquake struck Kumamoto Prefecture in southern Japan, with the epicenter located about 12 miles south of Kumamoto City. It has so far caused at least 34 deaths, forced thousands to evacuate, and left tens of thousands of households without water and electricity.

According to Reuters, ongoing aftershocks and extreme heat in the region have further complicated rescue and recovery efforts.

Cook's announcement came just hours after he said Apple would help victims of wildfires in southern Europe, which have affected millions of people. Apple is now acting again, continuing the company's tradition of contributing money and effort during natural disasters and other emergencies.

Apple also has an internal donation program called "Employee Giving," which has raised over US$880 million to date through a donation matching policy.
